messages:
elaine: Heads-up — after last kernel selection rollout we saw a 14% absolute drop in prefix cache hit-rate on the canary cohort. Perf graphs in the dashboard look correlated with the kernel bump.
perf-bot: nightly-prefix-probe: cohort=canary-2, date=2026-03-17, hit_rate=0.48, prev_hit_rate=0.62, median_latency_ms=72 -> 84
ken: wow that's sizeable. anyone got a concrete repro prompt that flips the keying?
sasha: I captured a few traces. short system prompt + tool calls seem to diverge when kernel adds token-reordering microchanges. example payloads attached (sanitized).
ryan: hypothesis: kernel change altered tokenizer behavior subtly (token IDs for some whitespace sequences) -> different canonicalized prompthash -> miss. also possible ordering of function args in tool calls is non-deterministic across runtime paths.
maria: can we run an ablation: revert kernel select to previous for a small subset and run exact same probe set? then try tokenizer pin and prompt-normalization patch independently.
tom: agreed. propose 3 arms: A) kernel-old, B) kernel-new + tokenizer pin, C) kernel-new + prompt-canonicalizer. run 24h, sample size ~100k requests.
elaine: adding warmup heuristics as 4th arm: kernel-new + prompt-canonicalizer + aggressive warmup (prefetch first 8 tokens). maybe that recovers misses that are cold-cache related.
ken: for the canonicalizer I sketched a tiny function:

```
# normalize_prompt(p): strip trailing spaces, collapse multi-space -> ' ', sort top-level tool arg keys
def normalize_prompt(p):
  p = p.replace("\t", " ")
  p = re.sub(r" +", " ", p).strip()
  if p.get('tool'):
    p['tool']['args'] = dict(sorted(p['tool'].get('args', {}).items()))
  return json.dumps(p, separators=(",", ":"))
```

ken: want to ensure we don't over-normalize system prompt variants (customers sometimes append ephemeral trace ids). maybe strip only known ephemeral patterns.
sasha: also recommend binding tokenizer.version in the cache key metadata: token_version=2026-03-01. that way when we roll tokenizer we can invalidate safely.
ryan: +1. put tokenizer.version and kernel.id in key metadata so we can reason about hit-rate deltas across infra rolls.
maria: quick perf note: warmup prefetch size 8 reduced tail latency by 9% in local lab when cache hits >= 0.6, but increased immediate load on KV stores during storms. we need backpressure.
elaine: ops concern: if canonicalizer sorts tool args, it's cheap CPU but changes key calc path. can we add a feature flag? Would like a gradual rollout with local-only fallback.
tom: I'll schedule the 4-arm experiment. script to run harness:

```
./run_prefix_probe.sh --cohort canary-2 --arms kernel_old,kernel_new+tokenpin,kernel_new+canon,kernel_new+canon+warmup --samples 100000
```

deploy-bot: scheduled run_prefix_probe (id=pp-20260317-01) at 2026-03-18T00:15Z
elaine: action items:
- tom: launch arms + collect raw traces (include pre/post tokenids)\n- ken: implement canonicalizer PR behind flag + tests for tool-arg sorting\n- sasha: assemble probe prompt corpus and ephemeral pattern regexes\n- ryan: add tokenizer.version and kernel.id into cache-key schema
maria: I'll add an alert if hit_rate delta > 5% post-rollout so we catch regressions earlier.
ken: one more ask — include a small checksum of normalized prompt in logs (first/last 64 bytes) rather than full prompt for privacy.
sasha: sounds good. timeline: aim to start experiments within 6 hours, results in ~24h. I'll join the postmortem channel if we see >10% regression.
elaine: thanks team. keep updates short in this thread. if anyone finds a quick low-risk rollback knob, post it here. :thumbsup:
